shorts.name: Pin tumbler lock
shorts.q: Why does only *your key* open your lock?
shorts.a: Five pins are cut in two and block the cylinder. Only your key lifts every cut to the same line, so nothing is in the way and it turns.

shorts.name: Hydraulic jack
shorts.q: How can one hand *lift a car*?
shorts.a: A small piston pushes oil under a much bigger one. The same pressure on ten times the area gives ten times the force, and a valve stops the oil flowing back.

shorts.name: Speaker
shorts.q: How does a magnet *make music*?
shorts.a: Current turns a coil of wire into a magnet, and the fixed magnet around it pushes and pulls it thousands of times a second. The cone moves the air. That is sound.

shorts.name: Seatbelt retractor
shorts.q: Why does your seatbelt only lock when you *yank it*?
shorts.a: Pull slowly and the spool turns freely. Yank it, or stop the car hard, and a small weight moves and drops a catch into a ring of teeth.

shorts.name: Door latch
shorts.q: How does a door *latch shut* without touching the handle?
shorts.a: The latch bolt has one slanted side. The strike plate pushes on the slant, the bolt slides in, and a spring snaps it back out once it reaches the hole.

shorts.name: Bike freehub
shorts.q: Why does your bike *click* when you stop pedaling?
shorts.a: Spring-loaded pawls in the hub bite into slanted teeth when you pedal. When you coast, the teeth slide past and each pawl snaps back down. That is the click.

shorts.name: Elevator safety brake
shorts.q: What happens if an elevator's *cables snap*?
shorts.a: A governor wheel senses the speed. Too fast, and it trips steel wedges that clamp the guide rails. The harder the car pulls, the harder they grip.

shorts.name: Combination padlock
shorts.q: How does a padlock *remember* its combination?
shorts.a: Behind the dial sit three wheels, each with one notch. Every number parks one notch at the top. When all three line up, a bar drops in and frees the shackle.

shorts.name: Clock escapement
shorts.q: What makes a clock *tick*?
shorts.a: An anchor holds the gears back and lets them slip one tooth for each swing of the pendulum. Every catch is a tick, and every slip gives the pendulum a tiny push.

shorts.name: Zipper
shorts.q: How do two rows of teeth *lock together*?
shorts.a: Each tooth has a bump on top and a hollow underneath. The slider is a wedge that feeds the two rows together at an angle, so every bump drops into the next hollow.

shorts.name: Click pen
shorts.q: Why does one click push a pen *out*, and the next pull it *back*?
shorts.a: Each click pushes a toothed cam past ribs in the barrel and turns it one notch. It rests on a high ledge one time (tip out) and drops into a deep slot the next (tip in).

shorts.name: Kettle switch
shorts.q: How does a kettle know when to *switch off*?
shorts.a: Steam reaches a small disc made of two metals. One stretches more with heat, so the disc snaps inside out and flicks the switch off.

shorts.name: Fire sprinkler
shorts.q: What *sets off* a fire sprinkler?
shorts.a: A glass bulb of liquid holds a plug against the water. Heat makes the liquid expand until the glass shatters. Only the sprinklers above the fire open.

shorts.name: Tape measure hook
shorts.q: Why is the hook on a tape measure *loose*?
shorts.a: The hook slides by exactly its own thickness. Hooked over an edge, zero is its inside face. Pushed against a wall, zero is its outside face.

shorts.name: Music box
shorts.q: How does a music box *play a song*?
shorts.a: Pins on a turning cylinder pluck the teeth of a steel comb. Long teeth ring low, short teeth ring high. The song is written in pins.

shorts.name: Light switch
shorts.q: Why does a light switch *snap*?
shorts.a: You squeeze a spring until the lever passes its centre. Then the spring flips the contacts together in a blink, too fast for a spark to burn them.

shorts.name: Escalator steps
shorts.q: Why do escalator steps *go flat* at the top?
shorts.a: Each step rides on two pairs of wheels on two tracks. On the slope the tracks keep every step level. At the landing they come together and the steps form a flat floor.

shorts.name: Tire valve
shorts.q: Why doesn't air *leak out* of your tire valve?
shorts.a: A spring holds a rubber seal on its seat, and the air in the tyre pushes it the same way. More pressure means a tighter seal. Pressing the pin lifts it.

shorts.name: Stapler
shorts.q: How does a staple *fold itself*?
shorts.a: A blade pushes one staple through the paper onto a plate with two curved grooves. The staple never folds itself. The grooves fold it.

shorts.name: Mechanical pencil
shorts.q: How does a pencil feed its lead *one click* at a time?
shorts.a: Three jaws grip the lead. A click slides jaws and lead forward together, a stop opens the jaws, and they slide back alone to grab the lead further up.

shorts.name: Can tab
shorts.q: How does a tiny tab open a *pressurized* can?
shorts.a: First the tab pivots on its nose and cracks a vent to let the gas out. Then the rivet becomes the pivot and the nose pushes the lid in. One tab, two levers.

shorts.name: Gas pump nozzle
shorts.q: How does a gas pump know your tank is *full*?
shorts.a: Fuel rushing through the handle sucks air in through a small hole at the tip. When the fuel covers the hole, the suction jumps and unlatches the trigger.

shorts.name: Train wheels
shorts.q: How does a train *steer* around a curve?
shorts.a: Each wheel is a cone on a solid axle. In a curve the pair shifts outward, so the outer wheel rolls on its wide part and travels farther. The train steers itself.

shorts.name: Lighter
shorts.q: Where does a lighter's *spark* come from?
shorts.a: A spring presses a soft metal rod against a steel wheel. Spinning the wheel shaves off specks that burn white hot, just as a lever opens the gas.

shorts.name: Ballpoint pen tip
shorts.q: Why does a pen *stop working* when you drop it?
shorts.a: A tiny ball sits in a socket and rolls ink from behind onto the page. Land the pen on its tip and the socket dents. The ball jams, so no ink.

shorts.name: Vending machine coin check
shorts.q: How does a vending machine catch a *fake coin*?
shorts.a: A gauge checks the size and a magnet holds steel slugs. The same magnet slows real coins by an amount that depends on the metal, and only the right speed reaches the cash box.

shorts.name: Skin-sensing saw brake
shorts.q: How does a saw know it touched a *finger*?
shorts.a: The blade carries a small electric signal that skin changes and wood does not. Within a few thousandths of a second a spring fires a metal block into the teeth.

shorts.name: Sewing machine
shorts.q: How does a sewing machine tie a stitch from *one side*?
shorts.a: The needle's eye is at its tip, so it pushes a loop of thread under the cloth. A hook carries that loop around a second spool below, and the two threads lock.

shorts.name: Railway switch
shorts.q: How does a train *change tracks*?
shorts.a: Two tapered blades, tied together, slide sideways. One closes against its rail and guides the wheel by its flange. The other opens a gap for the opposite wheel.

shorts.name: Two-chamber teapot
shorts.q: How does one teapot pour *two different drinks*?
shorts.a: A wall splits the pot in two, and each side has its own air hole. Liquid can only leave if air gets in behind it, so plugging a hole holds that drink back.

shorts.name: Glow stick
shorts.q: What *snaps* when you crack a glow stick?
shorts.a: A thin glass vial inside the tube. When it breaks, two liquids mix and react. The reaction hands its energy to a dye, and the dye gives it back as light.

shorts.name: Starter motor
shorts.q: What happens when you *turn the key*?
shorts.a: An electromagnet pulls a lever that slides a small gear into the teeth of the flywheel. Only then does the motor get full power. Let go, and a spring pulls the gear back.

shorts.name: Self-emptying cup
shorts.q: Why does this cup *empty itself* if you overfill it?
shorts.a: The centre column hides a bent tube. Fill past the bend and the tube becomes a siphon that drains the whole cup through the base.

shorts.name: Four-stroke engine
shorts.q: What happens *inside an engine*?
shorts.a: Four strokes, over and over. The piston sucks in air and fuel, squeezes them, a spark sets them off and the blast drives it down, then it pushes the exhaust out.

shorts.name: Airplane windows
shorts.q: Why are airplane windows *rounded*?
shorts.a: Stress in the cabin's skin flows around each window. At a sharp corner it piles up and a crack can start, so every window, door and hatch is rounded.

shorts.name: Train coupler
shorts.q: How do train cars *lock together* on their own?
shorts.a: Each car ends in a hinged steel knuckle. When two cars bump, the knuckles swing shut around each other and a heavy lock drops behind each one, so it cannot swing open again.

shorts.name: Car differential
shorts.q: Why can your car's wheels spin at *different speeds*?
shorts.a: The axle is split in two, and small gears in a spinning cage join the halves. Driving straight they ride along; in a turn they roll, so one wheel speeds up exactly as much as the other slows.

shorts.name: Record player needle
shorts.q: What does a record's needle *actually read*?
shorts.a: A record has one long groove whose walls waver in the shape of the sound. A tiny diamond follows the waver and shakes a magnet beside a coil, which turns the motion into an electric signal.

shorts.name: Ratchet wrench
shorts.q: Why does a ratchet only turn *one way*?
shorts.a: Inside the head, a spring-loaded catch presses against a toothed wheel. Pulling one way, the catch jams on a tooth and turns the bolt; swinging back, it rides up each slope and clicks over.

shorts.name: Torque wrench
shorts.q: How does a torque wrench know when to *click*?
shorts.a: A spring in the handle presses a small block square into a notch. When your pull reaches the set force the block tips over with a click. It only warns you: the wrench still turns the nut.

shorts.name: Door closer
shorts.q: Why doesn't a door closer *slam* the door?
shorts.a: Opening the door pushes a piston against a spring. The spring pushes back, but the oil ahead of the piston can only escape through one tiny hole, so the door closes slowly.
